home.title: Welcome to the ASCENC Project
home.description: ASCENC (Sustainability Assessment in Cities and Buildings in New Climates) aims to research the interactions between cities, buildings, and future climates to reduce the environmental impact of civil construction and adapt the urban context to ensure habitability and resilience.

about.title: About the ASCENC Project
about.p1: The ASCENC project – Sustainability Assessment in Cities and Buildings under New Climates – emerged from the combination of Igor Catão Martins Vaz's doctoral thesis with Professor Enedir Ghisi's research project. ASCENC is part of the research project "Sustainability assessment of buildings and urban centers", submitted to CNPq under the CNPq/MCTI Call No. 10/2023, coordinated by Enedir Ghisi. As a differential, it includes articles from Igor Catão Martins Vaz's thesis, which addresses the impact of climate change on the environmental assessment of the built environment.
about.p2: The project organizes its publications and tools into six integrated thematic axes. Each axis focuses on a set of methods, data, and applications in cities and buildings under current and future climates:
about.axis1_desc: Outdoor and indoor thermal comfort, urban heat islands, future climate files (morphed EPWs), metrics such as UTCI/PMV, and strategies for thermal conditioning and urban design.
about.axis2_desc: Precipitation indices (RX1day, RX5day, SDII, R20mm, CDD, CWD, R95p, PRCPTOT, SI), analysis of historical and future patterns, flood risks, and applications in urban and agricultural planning.
about.axis3_desc: Potential and sizing of rainwater harvesting systems (RWH), water performance under future climate scenarios, and economic and environmental analysis of residential and urban systems.
about.axis4_desc: Benchmarking and simulation of systems (electric shower, gas, electric boiler, solar with backup), INMETRO/INI-R parameterization, primary energy, and sensitivity to habits and future climate.
about.axis5_desc: Quantification of CO₂ absorption by carbonation in concrete and mortars, A1–5 boundaries and service-life scenarios, with implications for GHG inventories.
about.axis6_desc: LCA of materials, systems, and buildings; integration with local and global databases (e.g., Ecoinvent, SIDAC), boundary definition, environmental indicators, and comparative studies.

tools.title: ASCENC Tools
tools.intro: The ASCENC tools are interactive dashboards developed to support researchers, designers and managers in assessing the impact of climate change on the built environment. Each dashboard explores a specific thematic axis of the project, based on global climate models and Brazilian context data.
tools.desc_paimt: Interprets future climate conditions in Brazilian cities for thermal comfort and energy efficiency analysis.
tools.desc_paimp: Evaluates future precipitation indices to support decisions in urban drainage and water resource planning.
tools.desc_paimaa: Estimates electricity consumption for water heating under different climate scenarios and usage patterns.
tools.desc_paimrwh: Assesses the impact of climate change on rainwater harvesting systems in Brazilian single-family homes.
tools.desc_paimacv: Will integrate life cycle assessment with future climate scenarios. Under development.
tools.desc_paicacv: Quantifies CO₂ absorption by carbonation in cementitious materials throughout the building life cycle.

paimt.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Thermodynamics
paimt.description: PAIM-T is a tool developed to interpret future climate conditions in Brazilian cities. The main objective is to provide researchers, policymakers, and professionals with a comprehensive platform to assess and mitigate the impacts of climate change, offering accurate data for thermal comfort and energy efficiency modeling. For more details, access it directly on Zenodo.

paimp.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Precipitation
paimp.description: PAIM-P is a panel developed to interpret future precipitation patterns in Brazilian cities, based on data from the CLIMBra project and 19 global climate models. The tool offers precipitation indices such as RX1day, RX5day, SDII, R20mm, CDD, CWD, R95p, PRCPTOT, and SI, allowing for detailed analyses on urban drainage, flood risks, agricultural planning, rainwater harvesting, and other applications. The panel is free, open-access, and designed to facilitate decision-making in public policies and urban planning, helping to build more resilient environments in the face of climate change. For more details, access it directly on the Zenodo repository.

paimaa.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Water Heating
paimaa.description: PAIM-AA is a tool developed to support the assessment and optimisation of water heating in households. The tool assesses electricity consumption for water heating in different climate scenarios and provides key indicators and metrics to help decision-makers assess and respond quickly to climate-related challenges. Designers can compare electricity consumption in electric showers in different cities, modify user behaviour patterns, and assess the impact of future climate change. More details can be obtained from the dashboard or by analysing the parquet database available in the Zenodo repository.

paicacv.title: Carbonation and CO₂ Sequestration Calculator for Buildings (PAIC-ACV)
paicacv.description: PAIC-ACV is a tool dedicated to quantifying CO₂ absorption through carbonation in cement-based materials (concrete and mortar), integrating service life and end-of-life (EoL) scenarios. The platform enables analyses from a Whole Building Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) perspective, assisting in the estimation of the net balance of emissions and carbon sequestration over time.

paimrwh.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Rainwater Harvesting
paimrwh.description: PAIM-RWH presents the projected impacts of climate change on rainwater harvesting systems across 652 Brazilian cities. By combining multi-model climate projections with a daily water balance model, it evaluates the potential for potable water savings and system reliability in single-family houses under historical conditions and future scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5). Explore how regional variations in rainfall and climate projections affect rainwater harvesting performance, providing uncertainty-aware insights for climate-informed system design.

ges_research.line6: Climate change and the built environment
ges_research.line8: Rational use of water in buildings
ges_research.project1_title: Sustainability assessment of buildings and urban centers
ges_research.project1_desc: This research investigates the environmental, social, and economic impact of sustainable interventions in the built environment through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The main objective is to model the synergy of sustainable decisions at the building level and analyze their integrated benefits on an urban scale.
ges_research.project1_members: Enedir Ghisi - Coordinator / Deivis L Marinoski - Member / Abel Silva Vieira - Member / Rupp, Ricardo Forgiarini - Member / Aline Schaefer - Member / Liseane Padilha Thives - Member / Arthur Santos Silva - Member / Max Weeber - Member / Andrea Teston - Member / Andrea Invidiata - Member / Igor Catão Martins Vaz - Member / Taylana Piccinini Scolaro - Member / Rafael Almeida Flores - Member
ges_research.project2_title: Thermal comfort and user behavior in shared work environments in a subtropical climate
ges_research.project2_desc: The project studies the human dimension of energy consumption in office buildings, linking thermal comfort to occupant behavior. Through continuous monitoring of environmental variables and subjective questionnaires, it aims to develop simulation models that are more faithful to reality.
ges_research.project2_members: Enedir Ghisi - Coordinator / Ricardo Forgiarini Rupp - Member / Mateus Vinícius Bavaresco - Member / Candi Citadini de Oliveira - Member
ges_research.project3_title: Transforming Street Water into a Water Resource through Biotechnology and Infrastructure Innovation
ges_research.project3_desc: This research aims to transform roads and urban pavements into biotechnologically enhanced systems for filtering and storing rainwater. The system seeks to provide treated water from pluvial sources for residential and commercial demands, combating urban water scarcity.
ges_research.project3_members: Enedir Ghisi - Coordinator / Liseane Padilha Thives - Member / Vernon Phoenix - Member
ges_research.project4_title: Climate Adaptation and Rational Use of Water in Buildings
ges_research.project4_desc: This project focuses on the climate adaptation and thermo-energetic efficiency of residential, commercial, and office buildings in Brazil through computer simulations and material properties measurement. It also includes the characterization of end-uses of energy and water in buildings, aiming to support the development of performance and sustainability standards.

netuno.title: Netuno
netuno.description: Netuno aims to estimate the potential for potable water savings in buildings through rainwater harvesting. The tool assists in reservoir sizing and evaluates the technical and financial feasibility of the system for non-potable demands, such as toilet flushing, floor cleaning, garden irrigation, vehicle washing, and evaporative cooling.
